# DropSpace 1.1 Beta6

<!-- update-summary: Improves recovery, cancellation, efficiency and message clarity across settings, files, downloads, previews, sharing and background tasks while preserving the existing experience. -->

## Changes

- Clarify 68 labels and messages with 405 wording updates across the ten interface languages, covering settings, sharing, downloads, music and removal warnings.
- Remove 10 unused messages left over from older screens.
- Show the correct removal warning for files stored by DropSpace. External file references retain the warning that the original file will remain untouched.
- Apply the same settings migrations before loading, updating or resetting UI preferences. Preserve legacy update-channel choices and avoid rewriting unchanged settings on each load.
- Preserve the expected folder type while its source is missing, allowing the reference to recover when the folder returns.
- Check the expected file/folder type when reusing remote availability results and enforce the metadata cache limit across concurrent completions.
- Prevent an in-flight failed progress checkpoint from bringing back deleted download history. Allow a later recovery attempt when only part of the download journal was readable.
- Isolate DLC notification subscriber failures so presentation errors cannot change package transaction outcomes, block cancellation or escape progress timer callbacks.

- Keep a valid source preview visible when its optional cache is unavailable or unsafe. Discard cached descriptors with missing required metadata before they reach the UI.
- Reserve a new numbered output name when a directory occupies the requested filename, preserving the directory and its contents.
- Process orphan payload paths as traversal advances instead of retaining a complete tree-wide file list.
- Allow already queued Quick Panel and Music hotkey stop operations to settle during disposal without accessing a destroyed lifecycle gate.
- Reject an invalid nearby-share lifetime before starting network/listener ownership.
- Retain Handoff replay reservations through the full accepted timestamp window, including permitted future clock skew.
- Keep website requirements aligned with retained download links after rejecting incomplete release metadata and changing language.
- Optimize the separately deployed web receiver source to prepare each file once while preserving its existing encryption and integrity checks. This Worker source change requires its own deployment; the App release does not claim it is live.


- Reject a canceled module activation before allocating a native job or starting a worker.
- Bind staging cleanup and renewal to the active durable lease, preventing a completed handle from deleting a newly reused directory or recreating completed work.
- Preserve spent bandwidth tokens when unchanged settings are reapplied, while keeping live rate changes responsive.
- Release HTTP response bodies when an observer or redirect step fails before handing ownership to the caller.
- Keep an already rendered PDF usable when its optional cache rejects a destination; page cancellation still propagates.
- Fence delayed search failures by the current query revision, content and cancellation state so old errors cannot overwrite newer results.
- Check inline text cancellation and UTF-8 byte limits before allocating its encoded copy.


- Keep staging lease path lookup free of unrelated storage initialization, so another storage area's failure cannot block plaintext cleanup or replace the original share outcome.
- Close download persistence admission atomically with publication and share disposal completion; retain coalesced progress wakeups through shutdown.
- Enforce caller-specified Internet Share byte budgets before staging, and allow zero-byte directory entries when the transfer byte budget is exactly filled.
- Clear retrieval query failures after a successful refresh while preserving action feedback.
- Format bounded item-card previews without copying the entire clipboard body, and avoid splitting supplementary Unicode characters at truncation.

v1.1.0-beta.5 is the immediate upgrade baseline for this release.

## Validation scope

All four maintenance rounds and the wording review belong to this single Beta6
candidate, based on published Beta5. The first round passed 21 selected Infrastructure tests and three
managed DLC lifecycle scenarios; the second passed 16 selected Infrastructure tests,
two managed hotkey scenarios and two focused Node cases. These are per-round scopes,
not a claim that all cases were rerun against the final combined candidate. The third
round passed 17 selected Infrastructure tests and five managed preview/search
scenarios. The fourth round passed 18 selected Infrastructure tests and five
retrieval/card scenarios, including a share-cleanup integration regression found
against the third-round snapshot. Existing passing checks were not repeated without
an affected risk.

See the [first-round record](../../docs/dev/beta6-maintenance-20261031.md),
[second-round record](../../docs/dev/beta6-round2-maintenance-20261031.md) and
[third-round record](../../docs/dev/beta6-round3-maintenance-20261031.md) and
[fourth-round record](../../docs/dev/beta6-round4-maintenance-20261031.md) for actual
execution, retries and final validation boundaries.

The wording review passed the ten-language resource, placeholder, review-record and
change-scope checks. It added no functional or model tests. One existing static
check still fails because it expects older model-help wording; the same failure was
reproduced against the original source and resources. It is not counted as a pass.

Publication requires the complete Windows App/XAML build and final package,
runtime, offline-resource and checksum checks. These gates do not establish actual
GUI/system integration, UNC behavior, upgrades from Beta5 or deployed Worker/browser
acceptance. Long-text layout and the removal warnings for external files and stored
copies still need interactive Windows validation. No broad suites, model inference
or stress benchmark were run for the wording review.

Existing native heap stability limitations remain unresolved. A separate issue with
overlapping temporary-folder ownership and older file imports remains unresolved,
as recorded in the fourth-round limitations. Model/runtime bytes and execution settings remain unchanged. The Beta6 host-source
binding follows the owner’s publication request and retains the experimental-model
status; no new model-quality or native-stability approval is claimed. The [publication record](../../docs/dev/beta6-release-publication-20261031.md)
tracks subsequent Windows CI, packaging and publication results.
